content: To be afraid of life is to be afraid of death. And to be afraid of death is to be unable to live.
author: Alan Watts
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Alan Watts understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: What would happen if you met today's stress with steady acceptance rather than resistance?
